title: Prepare to move abroad with children and family
seoTitle: Moving abroad with children and family | EXOBASIS
description: Prepare child travel consent, school, care, pets and a suitable home. Understand the separate UK and UAE family-law questions before committing to a move.
intro:
Moving abroad with children means making a new life workable for people who did not choose every part of the decision. They need permission to travel, somewhere to belong and adults who know what happens next. A relative who depends on you needs the same care in a different form.

Whether you are leaving permanently or preparing a refuge from war or repression, begin with each person's rights and needs. Then bring the journeys, school, care and home into one plan.

sections.title: Give every family member a place in the plan
sections.body:
List who travels together, who might join later and who remains where they are. For each person, connect citizenship and residence permission with the intended stay. An adult's work or residence permit does not establish every dependent's right to enter, remain or work.

For a child, include the adults with parental responsibility, any custody or residence orders, passport arrangements and the intended school stage. For an adult relative, include their own wishes, ability to consent, mobility, treatment and the person authorised to help with decisions.

This makes the difficult dependencies visible early. If one person cannot yet travel, organise their support and the conditions for joining later rather than assuming the whole household can follow the same timetable.

If you are considering a birth abroad, establish the child's citizenship through parentage or place of birth first. Then ask separately whether that citizenship could support a residence application by either parent, and what each parent would need for any later citizenship application of their own. These are distinct legal routes: the child's status does not automatically give the parents residence or citizenship. Confirm the evidence, residence conditions and procedure for each step before making it part of your family plan. Adoption calls for a separate assessment of whether the child acquires citizenship through the adoption and on what terms. Keep any residence route for the adoptive parents and their possible later citizenship applications as two further questions, each with its own requirements.

sections.title: Settle permission before booking a one-way journey
sections.body:
England and Wales: a holiday exception is not relocation consent

The GOV.UK child-travel guidance requires permission from everyone with parental responsibility or from a court. It describes a limited exception: someone named in a child arrangements order as the person the child lives with may take the child abroad for 28 days unless a court order prohibits it. That exception does not provide general permission for permanent relocation.

A travel-consent letter should identify the trip and the other parent's contact details. Carry evidence of the relationship, and relevant name-change or court documents. For a permanent move, resolve consent or court permission for that move, including education and contact arrangements. Scotland and Northern Ireland use distinct family-law arrangements: a family case there needs the relevant jurisdiction's advice and orders, not the England/Wales exception copied across.

UAE: establish the applicable custody framework

The UAE Government's family-law guidance distinguishes the 2024 Personal Status Law from the 2022 Civil Personal Status framework and its implementing regulations. Under the former, a custodian's travel abroad with the child requires the other parent's consent or a court order; the court can require guarantees for the child's return. Custody and guardianship remain distinct, including responsibility for the passport.

Under the civil joint-custody framework, a parent cannot take the child abroad alone over the other's objection without obtaining the competent court's permission. A justified application for a temporary travel ban is also possible. Resolve the applicable law, actual orders, passport release and any restriction with a UAE family-law specialist before committing to departure.

A clear result from a financial-case enquiry is not clearance of a child-custody or travel-ban case. The UAE departure guide explains the wider departure context. Keep the final consent and orders in your emergency documents. EXOBASIS can organise the document work through residence and document preparation.

sections.title: Choose school and childcare before fixing the neighbourhood
sections.body:
Compare the curriculum, teaching language and admissions stage with your child's present education. Ask the school for the actual entry requirements, available place, start date, assessment, additional learning support and documents it needs. A school on a shortlist is not yet a place your child can attend.

Put the full cost beside the choice: admission and tuition fees, deposits, transport, meals, uniforms and any learning support. Read notice and withdrawal conditions before paying a deposit, especially when you are keeping a second base ready rather than moving immediately.

For the child, plan the first ordinary week as carefully as the flight. Who does the school run, who can collect them, how will they communicate, and how will they keep contact with important people at home? Discuss the change in terms they can understand and preserve familiar routines where you can.

sections.title: Plan for care needs and people staying behind
sections.body:
An elderly parent may need to move with you, travel later after a clinical handover or remain close to their established care. Choose the arrangement with them and their treating team, then confirm who provides daily support, how it is paid for and who responds to a change.

For a child or adult with continuing treatment, align the last appointment at home with the first receiving appointment, the medication supply and suitable accommodation. Keep an accessible contact route for each handover. The care guide below takes you through those dependencies.

sections.title: Include pets in the route from the beginning
sections.body:
Moving abroad with pets can determine your departure date and accommodation. Identify the species, origin, destination, transit and whether the animal travels with its owner or an authorised person. Ask the vet and carrier about the actual route before paying for transport.

For non-commercial entry of dogs, cats and ferrets into the EU from outside it, the European Commission's rules address identification, rabies vaccination, the relevant health document and, depending on origin and exemptions, antibody testing. When an authorised person accompanies the animal, the owner's journey must fall within the permitted five-day window. An unaccompanied shipment outside those conditions follows a different regime.

Confirm the carrier's crate, booking and handling requirements as well as the destination rules. Arrange a trusted temporary carer if your pet cannot travel on the same timetable, with responsibility for later veterinary and transport work.

sections.title: Make the home fit your family's daily life
sections.body:
A flexible furnished rental is often a useful first step: it lets you check school journeys, treatment access and the neighbourhood before committing to a longer tenancy or purchase. Confirm occupancy, pets, accessibility, deposits, utilities, cancellation and the person handing over the keys.

If you want to buy, begin with a household brief rather than a property advert. EXOBASIS can organise the search, viewings, an independent title and purchase review, contract and completion coordination, handover and care of the property while you are away. Local purchase rights, registry evidence and professional roles depend on the country; the FCDO buying-abroad guide explains the need for independent legal checks.

Prepare the first arrival: beds, food, transport, a working phone connection, access instructions and the first school or medical appointment. Those details decide whether the new home immediately helps the family.

sections.title: Keep the family functioning through the change
sections.body:
Agree what remains in the original country: property care, bills, contact with relatives and any return arrangements. If you are establishing permanent life abroad, review which temporary arrangements now need a durable replacement.

EXOBASIS can coordinate the family plan, organise the required specialist and document work, arrange the arrival and keep the responsibilities connected. You can commission the full family assignment or the part you need resolved first. Start with who is involved, where they live and the next decision you need to make.
